arxiv-1505-04150.title: Reinforcement Learning Applied to Single Neuron
arxiv-1505-04150.creator: Zhipeng Wang, Mingbo Cai
arxiv-1505-04150.description: Abstract This paper extends the reinforcement learning ideas into the multi-agents system, which is far more complicated than the previously studied single-agent system. We studied two different multi-agents systems. One is the fully-connected neural network consists of multiple single neurons. Another one is the simplified mechanical arm system which is controlled by multiple neurons.

arxiv-1910-01982.title: Order Acceptance and Scheduling with Sequence-dependent Setup Times: a New Memetic Algorithm and Benchmark of the State of the Art Journal: Computers & Industrial Engineering
arxiv-1910-01982.creator: Lei He, Arthur Guijt, Mathijs de Weerdt, Lining Xing, Neil Yorke-Smith
arxiv-1910-01982.description: Abstract The Order Acceptance and Scheduling (OAS) problem describes a class of real-world problems such as in smart manufacturing and satellite scheduling. This problem consists of simultaneously selecting a subset of orders to be processed as well as determining the associated schedule. A common generalization includes sequence-dependent setup times and time windows.

arxiv-2111-06828.title: Quantum multicritical point in the two- and three-dimensional random transverse-field Ising model
arxiv-2111-06828.creator: István A. Kovács
arxiv-2111-06828.description: Abstract Quantum multicritical points (QMCPs) emerge at the junction of two or more quantum phase transitions due to the interplay of disparate fluctuations, leading to novel universality classes. While quantum critical points have been well characterized, our understanding of QMCPs is much more limited, even though they might be less elusive to study experimentally than quantum critical points.

arxiv-2207-00998.title: The Replicator Coalescent
arxiv-2207-00998.creator: A. E. Kyprianou, L. Peñaloza, T. Rogers
arxiv-2207-00998.description: Abstract We consider a stochastic model, called the replicator coalescent , describing a system of blocks of k k different types which undergo pairwise mergers at rates depending on the block types: with rate C i ​ j ≥ 0 C_{ij}\geq 0 blocks of type i i and j j merge, resulting in a single block of type i i

arxiv-2311-07155.title: Sync Pure Counterfactual Regret Minimization in Incomplete Information Extensive Form Games
arxiv-2311-07155.creator: Ju Qi
arxiv-2311-07155.description: Abstract Counterfactual Regret Minimization (CFR) and its variants developed based upon Regret Matching (RM) have been considered to be the best method to solve incomplete information extensive form games. In addition to RM and CFR, Fictitious Play (FP) is another equilibrium computation algorithm in normal form games.

arxiv-2401-14182.title: De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory for kinetic equations with nonlocal diffusions
arxiv-2401-14182.creator: Francesca Anceschi, Giampiero Palatucci, Mirco Piccinini
arxiv-2401-14182.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Francesca Anceschi, Giampiero Palatucci, Mirco Piccinini. We extend the celebrated De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory to a class of nonlocal hypoelliptic equations naturally arising in kinetic theory, which combine a first-order operator with an elliptic one involving fractional derivatives along only part of the coordinates. Provided that the nonlocal tail in velocity of weak solutions is just p p -summable along the drift variables, we prove the first local L 2 L^{2} - L ∞ L^{\infty} estimate for kinetic integral equations.

arxiv-2602-12905.title: Adaptive Scaling with Geometric and Visual Continuity of completed 3D objects
arxiv-2602-12905.creator: Jelle Vermandere 1, Maarten Bassier 1, Maarten Vergauwen 1
arxiv-2602-12905.description: Abstract Object completion networks typically produce static Signed Distance Fields (SDFs) that faithfully reconstruct geometry but cannot be rescaled or deformed without introducing structural distortions. This limitation restricts their use in applications requiring flexible object manipulation, such as indoor redesign, simulation, and digital content creation.

pmc-11330981.title: The effect of reappraisal on the emotional regulation of shame in young adults with ASD and typical peers
pmc-11330981.creator: Meyrav Gaziel-Guttman, David Anaki, Nira Mashal
pmc-11330981.description: Young adults with ASD experience shame in social interactions, and if poorly mishandled, it may interfere with their attempts to participate in their social environment. One strategy to reduce shame is cognitive reappraisal, yet the efficacy of this strategy was not examined in ASD.

pmc-11392941.title: Latent profile analysis of family adaptation in breast cancer patients-cross-sectional study
pmc-11392941.creator: Zhangyi Ding, Yarong Fan, Enguang Li, Fangzhu Ai, Huixia Cui
pmc-11392941.description: When individuals face life pressure or significant family changes, individuals with better family adaptation can better survive the crisis. Although the influencing factors of family adaptation have been investigated, the application of potential profile analysis has yet to be found. This analytical approach can reveal different potential categories of family adaptation, providing new perspectives for theoretical development and interventions.

pmc-11497763.title: Separation of small extracellular vesicles (sEV) from human blood by Superose 6 size exclusion chromatography
pmc-11497763.creator: Jerome Nouvel, Gonzalo Bustos‐Quevedo, Tony Prinz, Ramsha Masood, George Daaboul, Tanja Gainey‐Schleicher, Uwe Wittel, Sophia Chikhladze, Bence Melykuti, Martin Helmstaedter, Karl Winkler, Irina Nazarenko, Gerhard Pütz
pmc-11497763.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are valuable targets for liquid biopsy. However, attempts to introduce EV‐based biomarkers into clinical practice have not been successful to the extent expected. One of the reasons for this failure is the lack of reliable methods for EV baseline purification from complex biofluids, such as cell‐free plasma or serum.

pmc-13093691.title: Scientific knowledge about dementia: From the Global South to the world
pmc-13093691.creator: Timothy Daly, Ignacio López‐Barrenechea, Paulina Vergara, Faheem Arshad, Avanthi Paplikar, Aparajita Ray Chaudhuri, Lucía Crivelli, Agustín Ibáñez, Suvarna Alladi, Andrea Slachevsky
pmc-13093691.description: Most people with dementia live in low‐ and middle‐income countries (LMICs), but scientific knowledge about dementia is dominated by Global North perspectives. This interdisciplinary article combines expertise from Latin America, India, and Europe, using a mixed‐methodology approach that incorporates expert discussions, a narrative review, and five illustrative case studies.
